summary: Try hoy tod (หอยทอด), a hot-pan shellfish omelette with crisp, lacy batter and a soft, eggy center. In Yaowarat, Nai Mong Hoi Tod is a long-running specialist where you can choose oyster or mussel versions and crisp or softer preparations. Eat it straight from the pan for the best texture.
whyGo: The contrast between crunchy batter and tender shellfish is a Bangkok street-food classic.
Nai Mong offers distinct crisp and soft styles, so the same dish has noticeably different textures.
Its Phlap Phla Chai location sits by Wat Mangkon MRT and works well as a Chinatown food stop.
bestFor: Shellfish and egg fans who enjoy rich, freshly fried food
Visitors exploring Yaowarat who want a specific dish to seek out
People happy to eat in a compact, informal shophouse
skipIf: You have a shellfish, egg or likely cross-contact allergy
You avoid oily or fried foods
You need confirmed step-free access, quiet seating or reliable dietary controls
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes for a meal and possible queue; this is a planning estimate.
cost: Recent Wongnai menu listings show small oyster dishes from about THB 100–120, with larger sizes costing more. Budget THB 100–300 per person for a dish; check the current menu before ordering.
hours: Time Out lists Nai Mong Hoi Tod open Wednesday–Sunday, 10:00–19:00. A current Wongnai listing shows it open until 19:00, but confirm the weekday schedule and holiday hours before setting out.
bestTime: Go near opening or for lunch to avoid the dinner rush and improve the chance of finding mussels; Time Out reports mussel omelettes can sell out before 18:00. Eat in if possible, since crisp batter softens in transit.
gettingThere: Nai Mong is at 539 Phlap Phla Chai Road, about 100 m from Wat Mangkon MRT station according to Wongnai. Follow current station signage and mapping for the short walk; the shop is in the Yaowarat area.
booking: No reservation process was found; plan for a walk-in and a possible wait. Call the listed shop number, 089 773 3133, to check hours or availability before making a special trip.
accessibility: The shop is a small shophouse with limited seating; recent visitor reports describe a compact, non-air-conditioned space. Step-free entry, accessible toilets and table clearance have not been verified. Street and shop access may be difficult during busy periods.
practicalTips: Ask for the crisp style (ออลั่วะ / o-lua) or the softer, chewier style (อ่อส่วน / o-a-chian); the terms and preparations can vary.
Oyster and mussel versions are available; go earlier if mussels are a priority.
The dish is rich and shellfish-heavy. Check portion sizes and current prices at the shop before ordering.
Ask staff directly about shellfish, egg, gluten, sauces and cooking oil, including cross-contact; no reliable allergen controls were found.
Carry some cash as a backup and use a map for the current route from Wat Mangkon MRT.
decemberNotes: Hoy tod is a year-round dish, and no special December 2026 schedule was found. December is a busy travel period; verify the shop's holiday hours and expect Yaowarat crowds, especially in the evening.
uncertainties: Published opening schedules may be stale or differ by day; December 2026 holiday operations are unconfirmed.
Menu prices change and vary by size; online listings are indicative only.
Specific access arrangements, payment methods and allergen handling were not confirmed directly with the shop.
